Petitioners file this petition for quashing of the FIR No.2/2021 under Section 406/498A/506/34 Indian Penal Code registered at police station Kanjhawala against them and the proceedings emanating therefrom.
2. The marriage between the petitioner No.1 and complainant/ respondent No.2 was solemnized on 12.06.2017 according to Muslim rites and ceremonies at Delhi.
On 23.05.2018 one boy namely Affan born from this wedlock.
However, due to matrimonial discord, couple started living separately since 08.12.2019.
On the complaint of respondent No.2 aforesaid FIR was registered against the petitioners.
The respondent No.2 also filed CC No.1699/2021 under Section 12 of the DV Act against the petitioner No.1.

However, during the pendency of proceedings, with the intervention of family friends and respectable members of society, the couple has sorted out their differences and settled all the issues and respondent No.2 has started living with petitioner No.1.
The parties also arrived at the settlement before the Mediation Centre, Rohini Courts, New Delhi on 18.10.2021.
3. Pursuant to settlement, the respondent No.2 has already withdrawn the complaint case filed by her against the petitioner No.1.
It is stated since the petitioner No.1 and respondent No.2 are living happily as husband and wife, the respondent No.2 is not interested to pursue the case any further against the petitioners.

4. The complainant/respondent No.2 has been duly identified by the Investigating Officer, states the Mohamad Arif & Ors vs State Nct Of Delhi & Anr on 18 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/108600548/

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 1 matter has been settled with the petitioners and she has no objection if the FIR is quashed.
The learned APP for the State has also no objection, if this petition is allowed.
The affidavits of parties are on record.

5. Considering the above settlement between the parties, there is no impediment in quashing of the FIR as complainant has settled all the disputes and has joined her matrimonial home with petitioner No.1.

In view of the above, there is no use to continue with the proceedings against petitioners as it would never entail in conviction of petitioners.
6.
Accordingly, the petition is allowed.
Consequently, FIR No.2/2021 under Section 406/498A/506/34 Indian Penal Code registered at police station Kanjhawla and the proceedings emanating therefrom are quashed.
Pending application, if any, also stands disposed of.
No order as to costs.

YOGESH KHANNA, J.
